To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Two polyubiquitins from Solanum bulbosastanum, bul427 and bul409, have different expression patterns and (2) The expression of both genes is wound-inducible in potato tubers and leaves.
Two polyubiquitins genes, bul409 ybul427, were isolated and their promoter regions sequenced.
(1) the S. bulboccastanum polyubiquitin gene bul409 is transcribed in potato leaves and tubers; and (2) the bul427 gene is transcribed in S. bulbocostanum and is also transcribed in potato.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation, structure, and expression of the two S. bulbocatstannum polyubiquitin gene promoters.
the identification and characterization of the genes encoding polyubiquitin proteins from the wild potato Solanum bulbocosanum and the expression of these genes in transgenic potato plants.
the development of transgenic potatoes that produce novel proteins in the tubers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of the bul427 promoter is not wound-induced in tubers and leaves, while the expression of the 409s is wound-induced.
the S. bulbocastaunm promoters are weak and inefficiently transcribed in potato, but are induced by wounding.
both the bul409 and bul 427 promoters are weakly expressed in tubers and are efficiently expressed in leaves and are wound induced in both tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) we have isolated two S. bulbocastaunm polyubiquitin gene, bul409 and 427, (2) bul427 has features suggestive of a psuedogene, (3) bul409 and 409s are transcribed in potato, (4) both S. bulbocaustanum promoters are weakly transcribed, but efficiently transcribed in potato tubers, (5) bul409s is wound induced in potato tubers and leaves, and
the S. bulbocostanum ubiquitin promoters are weakly expressed in tubers and are wound-inducible in both leaves and tubers.
the S. bulbocatstannum ubiquitin promoters were weakly expressed in tubers and leaves and were induced by wounding in both organs.
